Author: @futur3ndings651
Content: Within the first fifteen minutes there's already a potential glaring issue, and it's one I'm surprised wasn't brought up. Despite it showing as delinquency on the government site doesn't mean it wasn't taken care of. If you look into it further, the public records take time to update as there's a strenuous process of going through the IRS to verify as well as processing of completement of expunging the delinquency.  In fact in California specifically it can take upwards of three months, sometimes six months to update public records due to how long the process takes. So if the letter was sent out in May and he got it resolved a month or two later lets just say July as that's an entire process in it's own right, that means only three months have passed between those time periods. So the records may not reflect the actual status of the charity. I've seen videos of people getting pulled over and arrested for similar issues with their ID's and license plates despite the fact they already got them resolved, but due to lack of reporting and updating information into the systems, they still showed as unpaid/updated.
